correctness.rationale: Directly verified K=J(M D+)^2 and exact trace (a+b)^2s m(1-m), negative determinant -(ab)^2((1-m)^2-s^2m^2)^2. The unique positive root comparison to ab is equivalent to H<0. H is strictly convex in m for 0<s<1; small s give H>0 everywhere and s=4/c gives H negative at small positive m. Strict Perron monotonicity in s implies exactly one onset; compactness and positive H endpoints yield a single interior double root and exactly two optimizers at onset. An implicit derivative at zero gives (cs-4)/4. Exact checker run from included verify.py: 1383 test cases; numerical and finite checks are supplemental, not exhaustive proofs.

The broad four-phase existence theorem cannot imply the unique survival threshold and local/global paradox for every a>b; it supplies existence only, in a different cost-free model. value.rationale: A paired-block habitat environment has a qualitative global change absent from annual one-step alternation: optimal dispersal switches abruptly from complete isolation to an interior rate, before its marginal impact at zero changes sign. The uniquely defined cubic double-root survival threshold is a usable all-contrast structural benchmark for migration with mortality, not a routine evaluation of one arbitrary parameter tuple. Its value is theoretical, conditional on the explicit idealized model, and requires no claim of field calibration.
